text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and Thailand have signed an agreement on building a land transport corridor through Laos, giving people from mortheast Thailand access to Vietnam's Danang port via Quang Tri province.
-- The People's Prosecution Bureau in Hanoi on Saturday proposed heavy penalties for defendants of the Vietnam's biggest drug trafficking ring, with eight death sentences and eight life sentences.
-- In the first four months of 1997, 1,522 people died and 5,697 others were injured in 5,145 traffic accidents in Vietnam.
-- Phan Van Dang, chairman of the Liberation Union, former standing member of the Representative Committee of the Central Party and government in southern Vietnam died last Friday at the age of 79.
-- Disorder in exploiting natural resources in the northern province of Bac Can has reached an alarming level, creating waste, loss of resources, pollution, social evils and child-labour.
-- Hanoi has banned the use of explosives, chemicals and electricity for aquaproduct exploitation to preserve the environment and ecology.
-- The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development plans to tighten measures to protect and develop forests and complete inventories for the country's forested areas by December.

-- A $244.81 million project to expand Phu My power plant 2-1 in Ba Ria Vung Tau province, whose aim is to prevent power shortages in 1988, has been submitted to the Government by the Ministry of Planning and Investment.
